proof:
# Exact facet-cap tails for homothetic endpoint simplices

Let d>=1. Let K be a d-dimensional simplex of volume k>0, with
barycentric coordinates lambda_0,...,lambda_d. Let A and B be translated
positive homothets of K of volumes a,b>0, satisfying

    (A+B)/2 subset K, a=k+b.

Put these bodies at integer fiber coordinates -1,0,1, and let mu be
mixed volume on their union. Set gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d. For every i and
every closed ambient halfspace H whose middle trace on K is the
centroid facet cap {lambda_i>=1/(d+1)},

    mu(H)>=gamma_d k+2 gamma_d b
          =gamma_d a+gamma_d b.                  (1)

This includes every oblique extension of that particular facet trace.
It does not assert (1) for arbitrary continuous normal directions or
prove a halfspace-depth guarantee for the middle centroid.

## 1. Homothetic coordinates and exact endpoint tails

Write

    alpha=(a/k)^(1/d), beta=(b/k)^(1/d).

The translated homothetic fibers have barycentric coordinate forms

    lambda_i(A)=a_i+alpha lambda_i(K),
    lambda_i(B)=b_i+beta lambda_i(K),

where sum_i a_i=1-alpha and sum_i b_i=1-beta. Individual a_i,b_i need
not be nonnegative. Let

    sigma=(alpha+beta)/2, l_i=(a_i+b_i)/2.

The midpoint inclusion is exactly the containment of the homothet with
barycentric form l_i+sigma lambda_i(K) in K. Evaluating at its vertices
shows l_i>=0 for every i, and sum_i l_i=1-sigma.

The middle facet trace has a nonzero continuous normal. After multiplying
its ambient inequality by a positive scalar, every such halfspace can
be written in these affine coordinates as

    lambda_i(x)+t z>=1/(d+1),

for some real t. On the two endpoint fibers define the raw tail lengths

    r_A=alpha+a_i-1/(d+1)-t,
    r_B=beta+b_i-1/(d+1)+t.

They obey

    r_A+r_B=2h_i,
    h_i=sigma+l_i-1/(d+1).                       (2)

The simplex cap formula gives the exact endpoint contribution

    k[clamp(r_A,0,alpha)^d+clamp(r_B,0,beta)^d].  (3)

Indeed, a threshold q in the unit barycentric coordinate cuts volume
fraction (1-q)^d for 0<=q<=1, with zero or full volume outside that
range. This formula includes all threshold positions and saturated
endpoint caps. Closed boundaries are lower-dimensional and have
zero d-volume; d=1 is included.

## 2. Exact minimization over every integer coefficient

For alpha>=beta>0 and any real h,

    inf_{r+s=2h}
       [clamp(r,0,alpha)^d+clamp(s,0,beta)^d]
       =min(beta^d,2(h_+)^d).                    (4)

If either cap is saturated, the sum is at least beta^d. Otherwise its
value is (r_+)^d+(s_+)^d, which is at least 2(h_+)^d by convexity of
the function x -> (x_+)^d. This proves the lower bound.

For attainment of beta^d, choose r sufficiently negative so that the
left cap is empty and s=2h-r>=beta makes the right cap full. If h<=0,
choose r=s=h to attain zero. Finally, if h>0 and 2h^d<=beta^d, then
h<=beta/2^(1/d)<=beta<=alpha; choosing r=s=h attains 2h^d. Thus (4)
is an attained minimum, including equalities and d=1.

Since t ranges over all real values in (2), (4) computes precisely the
minimum over all oblique extensions of the prescribed middle trace.

## 3. The balanced volumes imply the uniform lower bound

The balance gives alpha^d=1+beta^d, so alpha>=max(1,beta). Hence

    (d+1)alpha>=2+(d-1)beta,

because the right side divided by d+1 is a convex combination of 1
and beta. Since l_i>=0, equation (2) yields

    h_i>=(alpha+beta)/2-1/(d+1)
       >=d beta/(d+1).                           (5)

For every integer d>=1 the binomial theorem gives
(1+1/d)^d>=2, so 2 gamma_d<=1. Combining (3)-(5) gives

    endpoint contribution
      >=k min(beta^d,2 gamma_d beta^d)
      =2 gamma_d b.                              (6)

The middle centroid facet cap has volume gamma_d k. Adding (6)
proves (1), with every factor of the volume normalization restored.
The total three-fiber mass is M=a+k+b=2a; thus the lower bound in (1)
is strictly greater than gamma_d M/2 when b>0.

If b=0 and a=k, the prescribed middle cap by itself has volume
gamma_d a, so the non-strict target follows directly. That case does
not require a positive homothet representation for B. No d=0
continuous facet-cap interpretation is claimed by this theorem.

## Scope of the result

This is stronger than the desired cap-sum inequality for this particular
homothetic simplex family, and it bypasses construction of one adaptive
coupling. It does not prove that a coupling attaining the proposed
multiplicity expectation exists, because a family of separate cap-tail
lower bounds does not itself construct a common coupling. It also does
not handle arbitrary middle-cap orientations, arbitrary endpoint shapes,
more than three integer fibers, or the general mixed-integer conjecture.
